desc:
Product catalog cleanup for online stores means finding and fixing duplicates, broken variants, missing images and unclear categories. Ecom Swift LLC reviews your products, lists every problem in a sheet, fixes them in your store and shows you what changed.

## What does a product catalog cleanup involve?

A catalog cleanup is a structured review of every product record in your store, followed by corrections. We look at titles, images, prices, variants, categories, tags and product status. Each problem goes into a sheet with the product, the issue and the proposed fix. Once you approve, we apply the fixes in your store.

Think of it as tidying a shop floor. Nothing about the products changes, but shoppers can find, understand and buy them without tripping over clutter.

## Why catalogs get messy

Catalogs grow in layers. A supplier import brings one naming style, a staff member adds products by hand in another, and an old seasonal range never gets archived. Nobody plans the mess. It builds up when several people add products over time without shared rules.

The result is easy to spot from the shopper's side. The same item appears twice with different prices. A product has no photo. A size option shows a color name. A collection holds items that do not belong. Each flaw makes the store look less reliable, and shoppers rarely give a second chance.

## How a clean catalog helps results

A clean catalog works on conversion through clarity. When a shopper lands on a product page and sees the right photo, a sensible title and working options, there is nothing to stop the purchase. Duplicate listings split attention and search visibility between two pages, so merging them gives one page the full weight.

Clean data also helps behind the scenes. Store search, filters, recommendations and feeds to shopping channels all read the same product fields. Fix the fields and every one of those features works better. Staff save time too, because they can trust that what they see in the admin matches what a customer sees.

## What a tidy catalog looks like

- One listing per product, with duplicates merged or archived.
- Every active product has at least one sharp image and a visible price.
- Variants and options match the real product, with no leftover or mislabeled choices.
- Product types and categories follow one clear naming rule.
- Tags are consistent, with no near-duplicates such as "tshirt" and "t-shirt".
- Titles follow one pattern and read naturally.
- Alt text is present on images.
- Drafts and discontinued items are archived rather than left half visible.
- Removed products redirect to the closest live page, so old links do not hit a dead end.

## How we work through it

We start with an export of your products and a read-only scan. The problem sheet comes back to you first, so you see every issue before anything changes. You mark which fixes you approve, and we never alter a live product without that approval.

In the Basic package we focus on the most common faults: duplicates, missing images and missing prices. Standard goes deeper into variants, categories, titles and alt text, and finishes with a before and after summary. Premium covers a full reset: rebuilt collections where needed, naming and tagging rules written down, redirects for removed products and a short staff checklist so the catalog stays tidy.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Decide on one naming style for titles, tags and product types.
- Archive old products instead of deleting them when you are unsure.
- Keep a backup export before large merges.
- Review the problem sheet yourself, since you know the range best.

**Avoid:**
- Merging products that only look alike but differ in material or size.
- Deleting a page that still receives visitors without setting a redirect.
- Fixing symptoms one product at a time while the cause is an import rule.
- Letting every team member invent their own tags.

## Who this service is for

This suits a store that has been running for a while and feels harder to manage each month. It suits a seller about to move to another platform who wants clean data to carry across. It also suits an owner who has just taken over a store from someone else and cannot tell which products are current.

## How to get started

Send us a short note on what bothers you most, even if it is only "it feels messy". We will ask for collaborator or staff access to your store. We do not need passwords, and you stay the owner of every product and setting.

After you order we reply with a checklist, run the scan and send the problem sheet for your approval. If you already know of specific trouble spots, mention them and we will check those first.
